html:
The Weapemeoc were an Algonquian-speaking people of the north shore of Albemarle Sound in northeastern North Carolina. The English who sailed to Roanoke in the 1580s recorded them as a chiefdom of several towns. Later they were known by the names of their smaller groups, such as the Yeopim, Poteskeet and Pasquotank.

English settlers from Virginia moved into the Albemarle area from the 1650s, and the Weapemeoc lost most of their land within a few decades. Their neighbours were the Chowanoke to the west and the Roanoke and Croatoan peoples on the Outer Banks.
